longlist.name: arimoclomol
longlist.reason: Approved product with an HSP70-induction rationale; no direct BUBR1 evidence, so a research hypothesis only.
longlist.first_experiment: Dose-response BUBR1 immunoblot with mitotic-timing readout in the same patient cells, at or below labelled exposure.

longlist.name: niacin
longlist.reason: Approved prescription product that feeds NAD; the SIRT2 to BUBR1 link comes from non-drug experiments.
longlist.first_experiment: Intracellular NAD+ and BUBR1 abundance in patient cells at a concentration achievable with labelled dosing.

longlist.name: gentamicin
longlist.reason: Readthrough needs a surviving transcript; other truncations suggest decay, and the label carries boxed oto- and nephrotoxicity warnings.

longlist.name: paclitaxel
longlist.reason: A microtubule poison acting on a cell already short of checkpoint function.

longlist.name: barasertib
longlist.reason: Aurora B inhibition shortens mitosis and weakens the checkpoint further.

longlist.name: HSP90 inhibitor class
longlist.reason: HSP90 inhibition lowered mutant BUBR1 abundance in cells, the opposite of the goal.

longlist.name: nicotinamide
longlist.reason: Acting as a sirtuin inhibitor it reduced BubR1 levels in reported cell experiments; not interchangeable with niacin.

longlist.name: everolimus
longlist.reason: Anti-anabolic effects are a concern in a child with growth failure, and the curated sources contain no BUBR1 bridge for it.

longlist.name: NMN supplement
longlist.reason: Supplement-grade, no approved single-ingredient product; mouse abundance data do not transfer to niacin.
